answer: Aggregate behaviour monitoring clusters each identity's recent outputs, compares them to a rotating reference set, and decays weight when submissions correlate too tightly. An attacker needs a per-identity bond, a price per attempt, a quorum of scored peers, and a rate cap stretching trust over days. A ring amplifying one voice fails because shared phrasing and timing register as a single echo, decaying every member's weight before payout; newcomers avoid that nebula of near-duplicates via separate meadow paths.
